claims.text: An on-the-fly actively trained machine-learning potential can replace a conventional EAM reference for multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
The machine-learning potential is trained or updated using ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations of the liquid at and near the melting point.
A Gaussian-process or neural-network interatomic potential is suitable for the proposed reference.
Conventional EAM references cannot adequately represent the extensive diversity of liquid-phase atomic configurations.
The actively trained potential will capture the diverse atomic arrangements in the ab initio liquid better than the EAM reference.
The actively trained potential will also describe near-melting solid-state configurations better than the EAM reference.
Capturing configurations underrepresented by the EAM reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
A reference potential that more closely reproduces ab initio interatomic forces under disordered high-temperature conditions will provide a smoother and more accurate thermodynamic-integration path.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's conventional EAM references.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is expected to decrease by approximately 50%.
The plausible reduction in path mismatch is estimated to lie between 30% and 70%.
The intervention will produce free-energy estimates that agree more closely with direct ab initio calculations.
The proposed temperature range is approximately 0.9 Tm to 1.05 Tm.
The intervention is applicable to equiatomic multicomponent high-entropy alloys such as CoCrFeMnNi.
The intervention may be less effective for lower-temperature, more ordered phases.
The estimated improvement is based on analogous success of machine-learning potentials in elemental and binary systems.

Failure to reduce path mismatch by at least approximately 30% relative to the EAM baseline, with discrepancies statistically indistinguishable within benchmark uncertainty, would falsify the hypothesis.
High-accuracy direct ab initio free energies obtained from extensive molecular-dynamics sampling are the proposed decisive benchmark.
